newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA PUNISH INDIA FOR MISSED CATCHES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOUTH AFRICA PUNISH INDIA FOR MISSED CATCHES.

text.p: India, trounced in the first test, were made to pay for missed chances as South Africa built up a commanding position on the first day of the second test in Cape Town on Thursday.

Gary Kirsten and Daryll Cullinan were both given "lives" and then punished their opponents by posting a record third-wicket partnership against India of 114 as South Africa reached 280 for four at the close. Their stand eclipsed the 60 Kepler Wessels and Peter Kirsten put on at Durban four years ago.
Kirsten scored 103 and Cullinan 77 after South Africa won an important toss in ideal batting conditions but India had only themselves to blame.

Luckless bowler Venkatesh Prasad saw Kirsten put down on nought by Mohammad Azharuddin at second slip and on seven by Anil Kumble in the gully. Cullinan was spared on 33 when V.V.S. Laxman in the covers was unable to lay a hand on a mistimed drive off the bowling of debutant Doda Ganesh.
The result was South Africa lost only one wicket in each of the first two sessions, with Andrew Hudson (16) and Adam Bacher (25) both giving catches to wicket-keeper Nayan Mongia.
Kirsten made his 103 in four hours and 50 minutes, hitting 15 fours to the delight of a 17,455 full house at his home ground.

Against a tiring Indian attack he might easily have bettered his test best of 133 but was finally run out off a no ball. He ended up at the same end as Cullinan but still was close to recovering his ground at the non-striker's end before the wicket was broken after Azharuddin's throw from short midwicket was relayed to the bowler.
Cullinan looked set for his century too in a fluent innings which included one brutal six pulled from outside off-stump and over the deep midwicket boundary off the bowling of Saurav Ganguly.
But he became Mongia's third victim when he gloved a bouncer from Prasad down the legside to the keeper.
Skipper Hansie Cronje (35 not out) and Brian McMillan (13 not out) saw their side safely to the close.
South Africa won the first test in Durban by 328 runs with two days to spare. It is a three-test series.
